_note: Phố, nước và một phần mốc trích từ OpenStreetMap qua Overpass API, đã đơn giản hoá (Douglas–Peucker 4–6 m) để chạy offline: không tile, không thư viện, không gọi mạng lúc dùng. Mốc du lịch chính, lộ trình và lớp tranh là nội dung tuyển chọn tay. THỨ TỰ MỐC LÀ HỢP ĐỒNG: route.js trỏ theo `sight:<chỉ số>`, nên mốc tuyển chọn phải giữ nguyên vị trí 0..N-1, mốc OSM nối thêm vào sau, và mốc bổ sung cho vùng cũ chỉ được nối vào CUỐI mảng. Đây là bản đồ ĐỊNH HƯỚNG, không thay bản đồ dẫn đường.

landmarks.note: The 18th-century covered bridge on the 20,000₫ note. Ticketed to cross.
Two-storey merchant house beside the bridge. Trapdoor in the floor for flood season.
Cantonese congregation hall. Red-and-gold courtyard, dragon fountain.
Working silk and lantern workshop. Short traditional music sets through the day.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Văn hoá Sa Huỳnh
landmarks.note: Burial jars and bronze from the Sa Huynh culture, 2,000 years before the port.
Seven generations of one family. Japanese, Chinese and Vietnamese joinery in one room.
The largest assembly hall. Dedicated to Thiên Hậu, protector of sailors.
Cham-era well down a narrow alley. Cao lầu is said to need this water.
Private ancestral chapel in a walled garden. Still used by the family.
Temple to general Quan Công, facing the market. Traders came here to swear oaths.
Produce in the morning, cooked food all day. The cheapest prices in the old town.
Where the paper-lantern boats launch after dark. Agree the fare before boarding.
Crossing to Cẩm Nam island. Chè bắp and bánh đập are the reason to walk over.
Western crossing out of the old town, named for a local revolutionary.
An old house open without a ticket. There is usually a shop inside.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Gốm sứ Mậu dịch
landmarks.note: Ceramics raised from the harbour and from wrecks — the port's reach, in shards.
The town's main history museum, from the Sa Huỳnh era to the trading port.
Neighbourhood pagoda west of the old town. Quiet, few visitors.
Where residents actually shop. Outside the ticketed zone, so prices run lower.
Fabric by the metre and tailors upstairs. Agree the price and the date in writing.
Lantern stalls and street food after dark, on the An Hội side of the river.
A former pharmacy and trading house. The family collection is upstairs.
The produce row of the riverside market — a place to buy fruit, not a sight.
Small neighbourhood temple. Name as recorded in OpenStreetMap; the sign outside may read differently.

landmarks.n: Nhà biểu diễn nghệ thuật cổ truyền
landmarks.note: Short sets of traditional music and dance through the day, on the old-town ticket.
Hainanese congregation hall, raised in memory of merchants lost at sea.
Teochew hall. The carved woodwork is the reason to step inside.
Memorial to the Polish conservator whose survey work helped save the old town.
The lane that lights up after dark. Busiest roughly 18:00–21:00.
A concrete blockhouse left from the colonial period, on the edge of town.
A 300-year-old Chinese merchant house, one room wide and very long. On the old-town ticket.
The footbridge to the lantern island. Where the paper-lantern sellers stand after dark.
The workshops that supply the town's lanterns. Bamboo frames split by hand at the front.
The town's Catholic church, a short walk north of the protected core.
The river island across the bridge. Chè bắp, bánh đập and hến trộn are made here.

art._note: Tranh vẽ tay dùng làm nền. KHÔNG phải bản đồ khảo sát: bố cục phố trong tranh là ấn tượng của người vẽ. Hai mốc dưới đây neo Chùa Cầu vào đúng cây cầu trong tranh và ấn định tỉ lệ + góc xoay, nên KHOẢNG CÁCH VÀ HƯỚNG GIỮA CÁC GHIM là thật; vị trí tuyệt đối so với từng mái nhà trong tranh thì không. Bản đồ chính xác là bản vector ở Open full map.
art.alt: Illustrated aerial view of Hoi An Old Town: tiled roofs, the Japanese Covered Bridge and the river

routes.name: Lantern Walk Route
routes.blurb: Wander slowly, greet locals, and let Hội An find you.

stops.tip: Visit at sunset for the best lantern reflections on the water.
Ask to see the flood marks on the wall — they go up past head height.
The courtyard is quietest just after it opens.
Agree the boat price before stepping in, and count the lanterns you get.

streets.n: Lối vào Thư viện Quốc gia Phố Tràng Thi
Quảng trường Cách mạng Tháng Tám
Quảng trường Cách mạng Tháng Tám
Lối đi nội bộ Chợ Hàng Da

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Công an Hà Nội
Bảo tàng Lịch sử Quốc gia Việt Nam

landmarks.note: The French colonial prison, later the “Hanoi Hilton”. Most of it is a hotel now; one wing is the museum.
The last of the old city's sixteen gates, built in 1749 and still straddling the street.
Friday to Sunday nights the main north–south lane closes to traffic and fills with stalls.
The oldest temple in the old quarter, guarding its eastern gate since the 11th century.
The beer corner. Plastic stools go out on the road from late afternoon; the road is the seating.
The 1911 opera house at the end of Tràng Tiền, modelled on the Palais Garnier.

routes.name: Hoan Kiem Loop
routes.blurb: One slow lap of the lake, ending in the old quarter.

stops.tip: Early morning is when the lake belongs to the neighbourhood.
The red bridge is busiest at midday.
Go for the food lane behind the market, not the market itself.

landmarks.n: Bia Kỷ Niệm Lễ Độc Lập
Bia Kỷ Niệm Sự Kiện Đấu Tranh Ngày 19/3/1950
Bia Tưởng Niệm Trận Đánh Tòa Đại Sứ Mỹ
Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh
Bảo tàng Mỹ thuật Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
Bảo tàng Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh
Di Tích Chuồng Chim Bồ Câu Người Ấn Tamil
Giáo xứ Chợ Đũi - Nhà thờ Huyện Sĩ
Miếu Năm Bà Ngũ Hành Tao Đàn

landmarks.note: The pedestrian boulevard from City Hall to the river. Busiest after 20:00.
A shaded lane of bookshops and coffee beside the cathedral.
The long park beside the market, and the terminus for most city buses.
The 1897 opera house on Đồng Khởi, between the two colonial hotels.

routes.name: The Colonial Spine
routes.blurb: Three blocks that hold most of what the French left standing.

stops.tip: Start at the market. Everything here is negotiable and the first price is not the price.
The cathedral has been under restoration for years — the outside is the point.
The post office still works as a post office. Postcards at the back, on the left.

landmarks.note: Steel dragon over the river. It breathes fire and then water at 21:00 on Saturday and Sunday.
The largest collection of Cham stone carving anywhere, in the 1915 pavilion built to hold it.
Food and dried goods below, fabric and tailoring above. Prices are asked, not fixed.
Where the city actually eats. The ground-floor food court is the cheapest hot meal in the centre.
Pink 1923 French cathedral with a rooster on the spire instead of a cross — hence the local name.
A swing bridge: the centre span turns side-on around 01:00 to let ships through, then turns back.

landmarks.n: Cầu Tình yêu · Cá chép hoá rồng
landmarks.note: A short pier of heart-shaped locks beside a carp turning into a dragon. The night crowd's meeting point.
City-centre pagoda with a garden courtyard, open through the day.
The Nguyễn fort that held off the first French attack in 1858. Vauban plan, low earth walls.
City history in the citadel grounds, including the 1858 siege and the American build-out of the port.
A single leaning mast holding the whole deck on cables. Lit in changing colour after dark.
Where the night river boats leave. Agree the price and the route before boarding, not after.

routes.name: Han River After Dark
routes.blurb: Market, cathedral, then the two bridges — timed to end at the dragon.

stops.tip: Eat before you walk. The market's food floor closes early evening.
The rooster on the spire is easier to spot from across the road.
The locks and the carp are the meeting point; it gets crowded by 20:30.
Fire and water at 21:00, Saturday and Sunday. Stand upwind of the head.

streets.n: Đường Khách sạn Mỹ Khê II
Đường Khách sạn Mỹ Khê II

landmarks.note: Open sand the length of the city. Lifeguards fly flags — red means the rip is running.
Vietnam's first floodlit night-swimming beach, open through the evening in summer.
The public end of the beach: showers, free parking and a lantern-lit square behind it.
The northern beach entrance, with the largest square and the most food carts after sunset.
Two blocks of bars, western food and late-night bún. The backpacker end of the beach.
The neighbourhood market behind the beach. Seafood here costs a fraction of the beach road.
The quiet southern end of the strip, below the hotel line.

landmarks.n: Nhà thờ Đức Mẹ Sao Biển
Tượng Phật Quan Âm - Chùa Mỹ Khê

routes.name: Beach Strip Morning
routes.blurb: Market first for the price you should be paying, then north up the sand.

stops.tip: Check what seafood costs here before you sit down anywhere on the beach road.
Coffee at the An Thượng end. The bars open late; the cafés open early.
Swim before nine. After that the sand is too hot to cross barefoot.
Showers and shade at the public park end.

landmarks.note: The walled palace city of the Nguyễn emperors. Enter at Ngọ Môn; allow half a day inside.
The five-phoenix gate on the 50,000₫ note. The centre door was used by exactly one person.
The tallest flagpole in Vietnam, on three stepped terraces facing the river.
Six spans of Eiffel-era steel over the Perfume River, lit in changing colour after dark.
Huế's central market since 1899. The cooked-food row is the cheapest bún bò in town.

landmarks.n: Bảo tàng Cổ vật Cung đình Huế
landmarks.note: Court dress, ceramics and furniture in a wooden palace hall moved here in 1923.
A royal pagoda on the canal, with a painted dragon ceiling uncovered during restoration.
The riverside pavilion where exam results were announced. On the 50,000₫ note beside Ngọ Môn.
The emperor's landing stage on the river, a few steps from Phu Văn Lâu.
The lotus lake inside the citadel walls. In flower from May to August.

landmarks.n: Phố đi bộ Nguyễn Đình Chiểu
landmarks.note: The south-bank river promenade, closed to traffic in the evening.

routes.name: Citadel Loop
routes.blurb: Breakfast at the market, the palace while it is cool, then out to the river.

stops.tip: Bún bò upstairs, from about six in the morning.
Buy the combined ticket here if you also want the tombs.
Both pavilions on the river bank are free and usually empty.
Cross on foot at dusk, when the bridge lighting starts cycling.
